note: Hand-picked recent AI reporting from large, reputable newsrooms, links verified. Source mix is limited by access tooling: WSJ, Reuters, FT and Bloomberg are blocked from automated browsing, so the openable/verified set skews CNBC, AP (wire) and MIT Technology Review. The updater (8×/day) can broaden sources over time.

items.title: Tim Scott wants to hear from Warsh on data centers and AI
items.blurb: Senate Banking chair signals AI power demand and its inflation risk are now central to Fed oversight questions.

items.title: Litigation could pause OpenAI's device plan
items.blurb: Apple's trade-secret suit threatens to stall OpenAI's consumer-hardware ambitions, injecting fresh legal risk into its Jony Ive device push.

items.title: Employees sue Meta, alleging AI was used to conduct layoffs discriminatorily
items.blurb: Current and former Meta workers allege the company relied on AI to select layoffs in a way that discriminated against them.

items.title: Cybersecurity stocks rally on AI-spending comments and Mythos rollout
items.blurb: Security stocks jumped after IBM's Krishna and Anthropic's restricted Mythos deployment reshaped how AI shifts enterprise security spend.

items.title: Wall Street warms to Apple's AI strategy
items.blurb: Investors reassess Apple's slower, partnership-led AI approach as its suit against OpenAI escalates.

items.title: AI is changing older workers' careers, research finds — here's how
items.blurb: Boston College research finds workers 55-plus in AI-exposed industries leaving jobs more often as automation reshapes late careers.

items.title: Meta's Louisiana data-center investment to reach $50 billion
items.blurb: Meta's Hyperion supercluster in Richland Parish will exceed $50 billion and 5 gigawatts, up from a $10B initial estimate.

items.title: U.S. IPO market poised to break records
items.blurb: U.S. IPO proceeds hit a record, with the biggest AI listings — Anthropic and OpenAI — still ahead in the pipeline.

items.title: AI executives say demand is 'almost unlimited' amid chip-stock volatility
items.blurb: Industry leaders push back on slowdown fears even as customers grow cautious on the cost of running AI at scale.

items.title: Goldman Sachs picks its favorite Chinese AI models
items.blurb: Bank flags cheaper open-weight Chinese models gaining US enterprise share as OpenAI/Anthropic costs rise.

items.title: Haves, have-nots and know-nots: Inside AI's new class divide
items.blurb: As Fable, Sol and Mythos ship under access gates, Axios argues a widening gap between AI's users, non-users and skeptics.

items.title: OpenAI power consolidates under co-founder Greg Brockman ahead of prospective IPO
items.blurb: With Fidji Simo departing, product authority concentrates under President Greg Brockman as OpenAI positions for a possible public offering.

items.title: OpenAI's Fidji Simo steps down over health issues
items.blurb: OpenAI's applications chief exits to manage a chronic illness (POTS), moving to a part-time advisor role after an April medical leave.

items.title: Inside the alternative playbook to AI regulation
items.blurb: As Washington leans on export threats and pre-release reviews, states and industry test a lighter-touch regulatory model.

items.title: Apple sues OpenAI alleging trade secret theft, says scheme was 'at every level'
items.blurb: Apple's suit names OpenAI's hardware chief over alleged trade-secret theft; Apple confirms its new Siri will run on Google Gemini, not ChatGPT.

items.title: SK Hynix rises 13% in Nasdaq debut. Chairman tells CNBC 'demand is enormous'
items.blurb: The HBM-memory maker closed +13% in a record $26.5B ADR listing; chairman says AI-driven memory demand shows no sign of shrinking.

items.title: The AI race is shifting from bigger models to cheaper, smarter systems
items.blurb: As frontier gains narrow, buyers route work to the cheapest 'good-enough' model, pushing labs toward efficiency over raw scale.

items.title: Apple sues OpenAI for trade secret theft
items.blurb: Suit cites 400+ former Apple staff now at OpenAI and its hardware chief soliciting Apple parts during interviews.

items.title: Meta stock logs best week since early 2024 as AI optimism builds
items.blurb: Meta shares rose ~15% on the week as investors warmed to Zuckerberg's aggressive AI spending and 14-gigawatt compute goal.

items.title: AI, data center fears could be key in closely watched Michigan Democratic Senate primary
items.blurb: Power costs and data-center siting become a flashpoint in a closely watched Michigan Democratic Senate primary.

items.title: Health system learning enables generalist neuroimaging models
items.blurb: Nature Medicine study shows training on private health-system data yields generalist neuroimaging models.

items.title: Meta updates its Spark model, releases developer version
items.blurb: Meta ships Muse Spark 1.1 and starts charging on a paid API ($1.25/$4.25 per M), its first move into selling AI access.

items.title: OpenAI releases GPT-5.6 and ChatGPT Work tool
items.blurb: GPT-5.6 (Sol/Terra/Luna) goes broadly public after the government hold lifts; new ChatGPT Work assembles docs across connected apps.

items.title: Transcript: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman speaks with CNBC's Julia Boorstin
items.blurb: Altman says GPT-5.6 Sol is 54% more token-efficient on agentic coding and details the government back-and-forth over the rollout.
